subject: POC Connectivity Sprint — API key rotation & VPC peering gating
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@aventishealth.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: procure+legal@aventishealth.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: POC kickoff & connectivity gating

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to move into a short POC focused on ingestion latency and cost at modest throughput. Before we schedule the first run, procurement and infra asked for a short checklist so they can provision:

- Org identifier and which Redwood account/environment we'll use
- API key creation process and rotation policy (we need a 90-day rotation outline)
- IP allowlist ranges they should open on our side for test runs
- VPC peering cadence and whether cross-region peering will be necessary

Can you share a mutual action plan (MAP) with dates? Procurement would also like to understand likely timing to sign a PO if the POC hits the targets.

Thanks — I can loop in our infra lead if helpful.

Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Platform Engineering Manager, Aventis Health
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@aventishealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & connectivity gating

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear list. I've sketched a compact MAP and next-steps below; attaching a working MAP spreadsheet (Aventis_MAP_v1.xlsx) with deliverables and owners. TL;DR: we can greenlight test runs within 7 business days if we get IP allowlist and org confirmation.

High-level MAP (week-by-week):
1) Day 0-2: Org bootstrap — you send target org_id, we create a tenant and share service-account guidance. (Owner: Chloe)
2) Day 1-4: API keys — we create scoped test keys, enable 90-day rotation flag; we'll provide a sample rotation script. (Owner: Chloe / Ops)
3) Day 2-7: IP allowlist & peering — your infra opens allowlist; optional VPC peering scheduled for lab if you need lower latencies. Peering checklist attached. (Owner: Aventis infra + Neha)
4) Day 7-14: Run baseline evals (latency/cost) and short report; if targets met, procurement begins PO. (Owner: Marissa / Ben)

Immediate asks from our side to unblock Day 0-2:
- Provide the exact org_id (or the preferred slug) you want Redwood to bind the tenant to.
- Send a short confirmation that Aventis infra will either 1) IP allowlist public egress ranges below or 2) request VPC peering. If peering, indicate the AWS account id and CIDR.

Security note: by default we provision test API keys with restricted scopes and a 72-hour expiry for the first run; once you validate, we flip to 90-day rotation policy as discussed.

Attachments: Aventis_MAP_v1.xlsx, vpc-peering-checklist.pdf (referenced inline).

Next steps: I'll loop Neha for technical preflight and Ben for procurement cadence. Want to tentatively target first baseline runs the week of Dec 1. Does that work?

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Hi Sanjay — looping in procurement cadence: assuming POC shows - latency < 80ms 95th and cost per 1k tokens within target, we can fast-track a standard PO. For timing:

- Standard Enterprise PO turnaround once legal buys in: ~7-10 business days.

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@aventishealth.com>, chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & connectivity gating — infra preflight

Sanjay / Chloe — quick infra preflight and sample allowlist values so your networking team can provision immediately. If you prefer peering instead of IP allowlist, we can do that but peering typically adds 2-3 days of coordination.

Required to run baseline (fastest unblock):
- Org id: outbound traffic should accept connections from these IP ranges (redwood test egress): 34.208.112.0/20, 52.204.0.0/16
- API key bootstrap: we'll post a one-time scoped key via secure link (72h expiry). After validation we'll flip to 90-day rotation and provide the rotation script (bash + terraform example).
- If you want VPC peering: provide VPC id, AWS account id, preferred region, and a contact for routing/peering acceptance. We'll provide the peering acceptance template and S3 presigned keys for TLS cert exchange.

Attachments referenced: vpc-peering-checklist.pdf (contains required routes, SG rules, and a peering acceptance snippet).

Quick checklist for Aventis infra to reply with (copy-paste):
- Will open IP allowlist? (yes/no)
- If yes: approximate firewall change date and contact
- If no: VPC id, AWS account id, CIDR, preferred region, contact email

Once we have that info we'll schedule the test key handoff and a 30-min technical runbook sync (Neha + Aventis infra).

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

- Procurement is attaching a PO draft and asked for your standard SOW (see PO_Aventis_119.pdf attached). They asked for a DocuSign link for signature.

On approvals: procurement is OK to proceed to PO once the baseline report confirms the latency/cost bands we discussed. I'll also add a quick note: if peering is needed after baseline we can stand that up in the following sprint.

Thanks — sending the PO now.
